profile.summary: BulkFormer is a family of foundation models for human bulk RNA-seq. A model takes one expression profile per sample, covering about twenty thousand protein-coding genes, and returns either a single vector that represents the whole sample or a vector per gene plus recovered expression values. Those vectors are then used as frozen features for downstream prediction, for example disease classification, prognosis or drug response.

Sample representations · Contextual gene embeddings · Expression recovery
The model returns contextual gene embeddings and expression predictions.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The three generations work differently. Atlas gives each gene a token that combines a learned identity embedding with a linear projection of log2(TPM + 1), then passes a CLS token and up to 4,096 selected gene tokens through 16 bidirectional transformer blocks of width 1,024 with 16 heads and SwiGLU feed-forward layers; the sample feature is the 1,024-dimensional CLS output taken before the projection head. Latest encodes all 19,973 gene positions at once: gene identity, a sinusoidal encoding of expression and a global expression MLP (19,973 to 2,560 to 768) are normalised separately and summed with fixed 1:1:1 coefficients, then a residual weighted graph convolution of hidden width 256 feeds a 12-layer Performer of width 768. A small network reads how much of the input is missing and applies a bounded gain and offset to the expression head. The published model of the preprint sums three embeddings per gene (an ESM2 protein embedding for identity, a rotary expression embedding of log(TPM + 1), and a sample-level MLP embedding) and passes them through three blocks of one graph convolution and four Performer layers at dimension 640. It is pretrained by masking about 15% of each sample's expression values with the placeholder -10 and minimising the mean squared error of the reconstructed values, and its gene embeddings are max-pooled to give a sample representation.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three generations sit in one repository. The publication family has five sizes: 37M, 50M, 93M, 127M and 147M parameters, with the authors recommending 147M where resources allow. The 2026-11-04 release added BulkFormer-Atlas (242.37M) and BulkFormer-Latest (154.55M), and on 2026-11-06 Latest moved to its final epoch-20 checkpoint. Each new model carries an immutable checkpoint ID: atlas-infonce-epoch10-update320000 and latest-20261106-epoch20-update148300. The repository is explicit that published PRIMO scores were produced by earlier checkpoints: Atlas appears as BulkFormer-variant, and the epoch-19 Latest as BulkFormer-V3Plus, whose scores do not evaluate the current download. A result should name the model, the checkpoint ID and the pooling protocol.

sections.title: Training setup of the published model
sections.body: The preprint reports pretraining on eight NVIDIA A800 GPUs for 29 epochs, about 350 GPU hours in total, with PyTorch 2.5.1, CUDA 12.4 and Python 3.12.7. The optimiser was AdamW with a maximum learning rate of 1e-4, linearly warmed up over the first 5% of steps, a per-device batch size of 4 and gradient accumulation over 128 steps. In its own comparison table the authors give an average single-GPU epoch time of about 96 hours for BulkFormer, against about 864 hours for Geneformer and about 16,128 hours for scLong. These figures describe the published model, not the later Atlas and Latest checkpoints, for which the repository gives no training cost.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Atlas: 16-layer bidirectional transformer, width 1,024, 16 heads, SwiGLU, CLS readout. Latest: residual weighted GCN plus a 12-layer Performer, width 768, 12 heads, with a global expression MLP. The published model in the preprint is a third design: three stacked blocks, each one graph convolutional layer followed by four Performer layers, embedding dimension 640, eight Performer attention heads. Its gene identity embeddings come from mean-pooled ESM2 embeddings of each gene's primary protein product, its expression values are encoded by a rotary expression embedding after log(TPM + 1), and a sample context MLP embedding is added to both. The gene-gene graph is a co-expression graph keeping each gene's top 20 edges with Pearson correlation of at least 0.4.

steps.title: Extract sample embeddings with Atlas
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import pandas as pd
from bulkformer import load_atlas, prepare_atlas_input, select_variable_genes, extract_atlas

model, vocab, normalization_vocab = load_atlas("model/atlas", device="cuda")
counts = pd.read_csv("examples/demo_counts.csv", index_col=0)
expression, coverage = prepare_atlas_input(counts, vocab, normalization_vocab, input_scale="counts")
panel = select_variable_genes(expression, n_genes=4096)
sample_embeddings = extract_atlas(model, expression, panel, batch_size=2)
print(sample_embeddings.shape)
PY
